discovery: Foundations of quantum networks: coherent light-matter interfaces for transferring and distributing quantum states between distant matter nodes

nominees.name: J. Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austria

motivation: Cirac, Zoller and Kimble established the quantum network as a physical concept: stationary matter qubits linked by flying photons through engineered, reversible light-matter interfaces. Their 1997 proposal for deterministic quantum state transfer between atoms in distant cavities, together with Zoller and Cirac's quantum-repeater and atomic-ensemble (DLCZ) protocols, turned entanglement distribution over lossy channels from an impossibility into a solvable engineering problem. Kimble's laboratory then realized the key elements: strong-coupling cavity QED with single atoms, heralded entanglement between remote atomic ensembles, and reversible mapping of photonic entanglement into and out of quantum memories. These ideas and experiments created a new capability, distributing and storing entanglement between material systems, that now underpins worldwide efforts in quantum memories, repeaters, distributed quantum computing and secure communication, including emerging industrial platforms. Their work combines conceptual clarity with quantitative experimental rigour, and it opened an entire field.
